eligibleLandGrants.name: USDA EQIP Ag Conservation & Irrigation Cost-Share
eligibleLandGrants.matchRequirement: Up to 75% federal reimbursement (90% for beginning or historically underserved producers)
eligibleLandGrants.purpose: Funding for micro-irrigation/drip lines, seasonal high-tunnel hoop houses, soil organic amendments, and erosion control windbreaks.
eligibleLandGrants.eligibilityCriteria: Agricultural producers with documented control of deeded land and gross farm income within USDA AGI statutory limits ($900k AGI).
implementationSteps: Obtain USDA Farm Service Agency (FSA) Farm & Tract number at local county service center.
Request free NRCS comprehensive conservation site assessment and soil moisture audit.
Submit Form NRCS-CPA-1200 prioritizing Practice 325 (High Tunnel) and Practice 441 (Irrigation Micro-System).
Execute 3-to-5 year contract and receive staged progress disbursements upon installation inspection.
eligibleLandGrants.applicationWindow: Continuous intake with quarterly ranking batches (State cutoffs in Nov/Feb/May)

eligibleLandGrants.name: USDA REAP Commercial Ag Solar & Energy Independence Grant
eligibleLandGrants.matchRequirement: 50% federal grant covering up to 50% of total renewable project costs
eligibleLandGrants.purpose: Installation of commercial ag solar arrays, ground-mount PV canopy over farm storage/parking, geothermal, and zero-emission microgrids.
eligibleLandGrants.eligibilityCriteria: Agricultural producers generating at least 50% of gross revenue from farming, or eligible rural small commercial businesses.
implementationSteps: Complete site solar insolation feasibility analysis and interconnection pre-study with local utility.
Obtain active SAM.gov Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) and CAGE code registration.
File USDA Form RD 4280-3A with verified contractor turnkey installation quotes.
Receive official federal grant commitment before purchasing solar panels or energizing system.
eligibleLandGrants.applicationWindow: Quarterly review deadlines: March 31, June 30, September 30, December 31

eligibleLandGrants.name: USDA Value-Added Producer Grant (VAPG)
eligibleLandGrants.matchRequirement: 1:1 dollar-for-dollar matching funds (cash, operational equity, or inventory)
eligibleLandGrants.purpose: Working capital to process raw harvest into high-margin branded products for Boutique Custom-Crush Winery & Olive Oil Bar (packaging, culinary extraction, label design, cold storage logistics).
eligibleLandGrants.eligibilityCriteria: Independent agricultural producers, farmer cooperatives, and majority producer-owned agro-ventures.
implementationSteps: Complete third-party commercial feasibility study and 3-year business pro-forma.
Document customer intent / purchase orders from regional wholesalers, restaurants, or estate retail.
Submit comprehensive grant application via Grants.gov during the annual federal cycle.
Deploy funds to cover processing payroll, certified packaging, and retail brand launch.
eligibleLandGrants.applicationWindow: Annual competitive window (typically closes in April/May)

eligibleLandGrants.name: California CDFA Healthy Soils Program (HSP) Incentives
eligibleLandGrants.agency: California Department of Food and Agriculture (CDFA)
eligibleLandGrants.matchRequirement: Zero matching requirement (100% direct grant disbursement)
eligibleLandGrants.purpose: Incentive payments for compost application, multi-species cover cropping, biochar soil integration, and hedgerow planting.
eligibleLandGrants.eligibilityCriteria: California agricultural operations with soil carbon sequestration management commitments.
implementationSteps: Use the CDFA COMET-Planner tool to quantify estimated greenhouse gas reductions on the parcel.
Submit project work plan through CDFA electronic portal.
Execute agreement and implement practices; submit annual soil carbon lab tests for grant payouts.
eligibleLandGrants.applicationWindow: Annual winter/spring solicitation
